terminal.description: A shell in your workspace where the demo indexes the handbook and searches it with your store.

tasks.title: Index the chunks
tasks.description:
Implement `indexChunks(chunks, client)` in `src/store.ts`. It returns `Promise<Entry[]>`, one `{ chunk, vector }` per chunk, in the same order:

- `chunk` is the chunk object, unchanged.
- `vector` is the embedding of `chunk.text`.
- Embed all the texts with one call to `embed` from `embed.ts`, which already batches them (29 chunks take 2 requests).
- An empty list gives `[]`.

The check indexes the handbook at chunk size 200 with overlap 40 and watches the requests you send.
nextSteps: Run `node src/demo.ts` and read the error for indexChunks.
Collect the text of every chunk and embed them in one call.
Pair each chunk with the vector at the same position.
Run the demo and check how many chunks were indexed.
hints: embed() from embed.ts is already written and returns vectors in the order of its texts.
Calling embed inside a loop would send one request per chunk. Build the list of texts first.
After one embed call over all texts, a map over chunks with its position gives you each { chunk, vector }.

tasks.title: Search for the top k
tasks.description:
Implement `search(index, question, k, minScore = 0, client)` in `src/store.ts`. It returns `Promise<Hit[]>`:

- Embed the question with one request. The index already holds the chunk vectors.
- Score every entry with `cosine(questionVector, entry.vector)`.
- Return the best `k` as `{ chunk, score }`, highest score first. `k` larger than the index returns everything; `k` of 0 returns `[]`.
- Do not reorder or change `index` itself.

Leave `minScore` for the next task. The check searches the handbook for several questions and values of `k` and compares chunk ids and scores.
nextSteps: Embed the question and keep its vector.
Turn every entry into a hit with its score.
Sort the hits and keep the first k.
Run the demo and read the top 3 for each question.
hints: embed() takes a list, so wrap the question in an array and take the first vector back.
Array.prototype.sort changes the array it is called on. Make sure that array is your new list of hits, not the index.
Map entries to { chunk, score }, sort by score from high to low, then slice from 0 to k.

tasks.title: Say nothing when nothing matches
tasks.description:
Top k always returns k chunks, even for a question the handbook never mentions. Use the `minScore` parameter of `search`:

- Drop every hit whose score is below `minScore`. A score equal to `minScore` stays.
- Then return at most `k` of what is left, highest first.
- With the default `minScore` of 0, nothing changes.

The check asks about surfboards (every chunk scores below 0.2), checks a question that keeps only some of its hits at 0.2, tries a cut-off equal to the best score, and type-checks `src/store.ts`.
nextSteps: Run the demo and compare the two blocks of results.
Filter the hits by score before you take the top k.
Run the demo again: the surfboard question should find nothing at 0.2.
hints: Filtering before or after sorting gives the same hits; filtering before slicing is what matters.
Read the task again for the word 'equal'.
Add a filter that keeps hits with score >= minScore, between building the hits and slicing to k.
